learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.

Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering in the specific Mechanical technology.

Possess the ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge about: linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithms; statistics and optimization.
Know and apply the concepts of vector spaces, linear systems, matrices and determinants, diagonalization of matrices, scalar product.
Know the concepts of real number, real functions of a real variable, limit, derivation. Be able to graphically represent real functions of one variable.
Be able to apply Calculus to examples typical of Engineering.

syllabus_topics: Sets and mappings; real numbers and complex numbers.
Real functions of a real variable, definitions, composition, limits and continuity.
Real functions of a real variable, derivation, chain rule. Rolle's and Mean Value theorems. Calculation of extrema. Taylor polynomials. Approximate solution of non-linear equations.
Vector spaces, subspaces, linear span, linear dependence and independence. Bases and dimensions.
Linear applications, coordinate expression of a linear application, diagonalization.

assessment_methods.method: Exam with supporting material (Differential Calculus in one variable)

assessment_rules: The final grade is based on two exams: Differential Calculus (60%) and Linear Algebra (40%). Both exams are recoverable. A minimum grade of 0 is required for each component.
